question: Joseph Francois Dupleix was the Governor General of which of the following East India companies in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is French.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Joseph François Dupleix was the Governor-General of the French East India Company in India, with his headquarters at Pondicherry. (डूप्ले — फ्रांसीसी गवर्नर जनरल)

 

• He served in this capacity from 1742 to 1754 and is best known for introducing the policy of alliances with local Indian rulers and using trained sepoys to further French colonial interests.

 

• He was a key figure in the Carnatic Wars against the British East India Company, fighting to establish French dominance in South India.

 

• He was recalled to France in 1754 after the French government sought peace with the British, ending his ambitious plans for a French empire in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The French East India Company was established in 1664 and set up its main base at Pondicherry in 1673.

 

• Dupleix's rival on the British side was Robert Clive, who eventually outmanoeuvred the French in the Carnatic Wars.

 

NOTE

 

• Dutch (Option 1): The Dutch East India Company (VOC) operated mainly from Pulicat and later Nagapattinam, and had no Governor-General named Dupleix.

 

• English (Option 3): The English (British) East India Company was headed by Governors/Governors-General such as Robert Clive and Warren Hastings, not Dupleix.

 

• Portuguese (Option 4): The Portuguese established their colonial base at Goa; Dupleix had no association with the Portuguese administration.

question: Indian sportsperson Praveen Chithravel who missed out on a medal at Commonwealth Games 2022 but made a strong comeback to win silver at the Asian Championships with a national indoor record is associated with which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Triple jump indoor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Praveen Chithravel is an Indian triple jumper from Tamil Nadu who set a national indoor record in triple jump while winning a silver medal at the Asian Indoor Athletics Championships. (प्रवीण चित्रवेल — ट्रिपल जंप)

 

• He missed a podium finish at the Commonwealth Games 2022 in Birmingham, finishing fifth in the men's triple jump final.

 

• He is a protégé of the Reliance Foundation's athletics programme and is considered one of India's most promising young triple jumpers.

 

• He is coached under the guidance of renowned coaches associated with developing triple jump talent in India, following in the footsteps of seniors like Arpinder Singh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other prominent triple jumpers include Arpinder Singh, who won gold at the 2018 Asian Games.

 

• The Asian Athletics Championships/Asian Indoor Championships are organised by the Asian Athletics Association (AAA).

 

NOTE

 

• Shot put indoor (Option 2): This is a distinct throwing event; Praveen Chithravel is not associated with shot put.

 

• Long jump indoor (Option 3): Long jump is a related but separate horizontal jump event; his specialization is triple jump, not long jump.

 

• 800 m indoor (Option 4): This is a middle-distance running event, unrelated to Praveen Chithravel's field event specialization.

question: Final goods are divided into:
solution_text:
The correct answer is consumption goods and capital goods.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Final goods are those goods that are used either for final consumption or for investment, and are not meant for resale or further processing. (अंतिम वस्तुएं — उपभोग एवं पूंजीगत वस्तुएं)

 

• Final goods are classified into two broad categories: consumption goods, which directly satisfy human wants (e.g., bread, clothes), and capital goods, which are used in the production process (e.g., machinery, tools) and are not consumed immediately.

 

• Unlike intermediate goods (used up in the production of other goods within the same year), final goods represent the end use of production in the economy and are counted while calculating National Income/GDP.

 

• This distinction is central to National Income Accounting, since only the value of final goods (not intermediate goods) is included to avoid double counting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Intermediate goods, in contrast, are goods used as raw material or inputs for producing other goods, and are excluded from GDP calculation to avoid double counting.

 

• Capital goods contribute to Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF) in the economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Raw materials and semi-finished goods (Option 1): This is a classification associated with intermediate goods, not final goods.

 

• Single goods and composite goods (Option 2): This is not a standard economic classification of final goods.

 

• War goods and civilian goods (Option 4): This is not a recognized economic classification used for final goods.

question: Neena Prasad was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2021 for her contribution to _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Neena Prasad is a renowned exponent of Mohiniyattam, the classical dance form of Kerala, and was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2021 for her contribution to this dance form. (नीना प्रसाद — मोहिनीअट्टम)

 

• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form that originated in Kerala, characterized by graceful, swaying movements performed by female dancers, and its name literally means "dance of the enchantress."

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is India's highest award given to practicing artists in the field of music, dance, and drama, conferred by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance and Drama.

 

• Neena Prasad has trained under legendary gurus of Mohiniyattam and has been instrumental in popularizing the art form nationally and internationally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in 1952 and is headquartered in New Delhi.

 

• Other classical dance forms of India include Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Kathak (North India), Kathakali (Kerala), Manipuri (Manipur), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 1): This classical dance form originated in Tamil Nadu, not associated with Neena Prasad's award.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 3): This classical dance form originated in Andhra Pradesh, a different dance tradition.

 

• Odissi (Option 4): This classical dance form originated in Odisha, unrelated to Neena Prasad's specialization.

question: Pawl Kut is a thanksgiving festival of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pawl Kut is a major thanksgiving/harvest festival celebrated by the people of Mizoram, marking the end of the harvest season. (पावल कुट — मिजोरम)

 

• It is celebrated in December, after the harvesting and threshing of crops is completed, as an expression of gratitude for a good harvest.

 

• The festival involves traditional feasting, folk dances (such as Cheraw, the bamboo dance), and community gatherings that highlight Mizo culture and tribal traditions.

 

• 'Kut' in the Mizo language means 'festival', and Mizoram celebrates several Kut festivals through the year corresponding to different agricultural stages, of which Pawl Kut is the harvest/thanksgiving festival.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important Kut festivals of Mizoram include Chapchar Kut (celebrated in spring, marking the beginning of the agricultural season) and Mim Kut (a maize harvest festival).

 

• The famous Cheraw (bamboo) dance is a hallmark of Mizo festivals, including Pawl Kut.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Kerala's major harvest festival is Onam, not Pawl Kut.

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Gujarat's notable festivals include Navratri and Uttarayan (kite festival), unrelated to Pawl Kut.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 4): Himachal Pradesh celebrates festivals like Kullu Dussehra; Pawl Kut is not associated with this state.

question: Which of the following is an INCORRECT statement in regard to the meaning of 'Union of States' in the Indian context?
option_1: Country was divided into different states for administrative convenience.
option_2: Indian federation was the result of an agreement by sovereign units to join it.
option_3: Enumerates the power of centre and states through various lists.
option_4: Federation not being the result of agreement, no state has a right to secede from it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian federation was the result of an agreement by sovereign units to join it.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 1 of the Indian Constitution describes India as a 'Union of States' rather than a 'Federation of States'. (यूनियन ऑफ स्टेट्स — संघीकरण नहीं, विभाजन)

 

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar explained that the term 'Union' was deliberately chosen because the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among sovereign, independent states (unlike the USA, where independent states came together voluntarily to form a federation).

 

• Since it was not formed by agreement, no state has the right to secede from the Union; the country was integrated into a single union through a process of internal administrative division, not through a voluntary compact between pre-existing sovereign units.

 

• The Constitution enumerates the distribution of powers between the Centre and States through the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List in the Seventh Schedule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The phrase 'Union of States' emphasizes indestructibility of the Union combined with destructibility of individual states — Parliament can alter state boundaries, but the Union itself is indestructible.

 

• This concept was elaborated by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar during the Constituent Assembly debates.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: This is a correct statement — India's states were created for administrative convenience, not as pre-existing sovereign entities.

 

• Option 3: This is a correct statement — the Seventh Schedule enumerates Centre-State powers via the Union, State, and Concurrent Lists.

 

• Option 4: This is a correct statement — since the federation was not formed by agreement, states have no right to secede.

question: Which German chemist used the technique of preparing hydrocarbons by electrolysis of solutions of salts of fatty acids?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hermann Kolbe.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hermann Kolbe, a German chemist, developed the Kolbe electrolysis method, in which hydrocarbons are prepared by the electrolysis of aqueous solutions of alkali metal salts of carboxylic (fatty) acids. (कोल्बे इलेक्ट्रोलिसिस — हरमन कोल्बे)

 

• In this process, the carboxylate anions are oxidized at the anode, releasing carbon dioxide and forming free radicals that combine to give a hydrocarbon (typically an alkane with double the number of carbon atoms of the acid used).

 

• Kolbe made significant contributions to organic chemistry, including the first synthesis of acetic acid from inorganic materials, disproving vitalism.

 

• He is also known for the Kolbe-Schmitt reaction, used industrially to synthesize salicylic acid (a precursor to aspirin).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kolbe-Schmitt reaction converts sodium phenoxide and carbon dioxide into salicylic acid under high pressure and temperature.

 

• Kolbe is regarded as one of the founders of modern organic chemistry in the 19th century.

 

NOTE

 

• Cecilia Payne (Option 1): She was a British-American astronomer/astrophysicist, known for discovering that stars are composed mainly of hydrogen and helium, unrelated to organic chemistry.

 

• Marcellin Berthelot (Option 2): A French chemist known for organic synthesis (e.g., synthesizing methane and acetylene) and for coining the term 'organic chemistry', but not associated with this electrolysis technique.

 

• Giulio Natta (Option 3): An Italian chemist known for his work on polymers (Ziegler-Natta catalysts), for which he won the Nobel Prize, unrelated to Kolbe electrolysis.

question: Which five year plan in India is referred to as the Mahalanobis Plan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2nd Five Year Plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961) is popularly known as the Mahalanobis Plan, as it was formulated based on a statistical model developed by the eminent statistician Prof. P.C. Mahalanobis. (महालनोबिस योजना — द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• The plan emphasized rapid industrialization, particularly the development of heavy and basic industries, laying the foundation for public sector-led industrial growth in India.

 

• Prof. Mahalanobis was the founder of the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) and is regarded as the father of statistics in India.

 

• The plan aimed at a socialist pattern of society and gave priority to capital goods industries over consumer goods industries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Five Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on agriculture and was based on the Harrod-Domar model.

 

• The Third Five Year Plan (1961-1966) aimed at making the economy self-reliant, but was disrupted by wars with China (1962) and Pakistan (1965) and successive droughts.

 

NOTE

 

• 4th Five Year Plan (Option 1): This plan (1969-1974) focused on the objectives of 'growth with stability' and 'progressive achievement of self-reliance'.

 

• 1st Five Year Plan (Option 3): This was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model, focused on agriculture, not the Mahalanobis model.

 

• 3rd Five Year Plan (Option 4): This plan (1961-1966) aimed at making the economy self-reliant but is not called the Mahalanobis Plan.

question: Who among the following founded the Indian Association along with Anand Mohan Bose?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surendranath Banerjee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Association was founded in 1876 in Calcutta by Surendranath Banerjee along with Anand Mohan Bose. (इंडियन एसोसिएशन — सुरेंद्रनाथ बनर्जी)

 

• It was one of the earliest Indian political organizations, aimed at creating a strong public opinion on political questions and unifying Indians on a common political platform.

 

• Surendranath Banerjee, often called 'Rashtraguru' or 'Indian Surendranath', was also famously associated with protesting against his removal from the Indian Civil Service (ICS) due to racial discrimination, which fueled his political activism.

 

• The Indian Association later played a key role in organizing the first session of the Indian National Conference (1883) and eventually merged much of its work into the Indian National Congress founded in 1885.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Surendranath Banerjee also founded the Ripon College (now Surendranath College) in Calcutta.

 

• The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by Allan Octavian Hume, with Surendranath Banerjee among its early prominent leaders.

 

NOTE

 

• Dada Bhai Naoroji (Option 1): He founded the East India Association in London (1866) and is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'.

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Option 2): He founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 and was a moderate leader of the Congress.

 

• Pheroz Shah Mehta (Option 3): He was a founder of the Bombay Presidency Association (1885), not the Indian Association.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct about the value of money?

i. It is directly related to the price level.

ii. It is not related to the price level.

iii. It is indirectly related to the price level.
option_1: None of the statements are correct
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only iii is correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The value of money refers to its purchasing power — the quantity of goods and services that a unit of money can buy. (मुद्रा का मूल्य — मूल्य स्तर से व्युत्क्रम संबंध)

 

• The value of money is inversely (indirectly) related to the price level: when the general price level rises (inflation), the purchasing power (value) of money falls, and when the price level falls (deflation), the value of money rises.

 

• This inverse relationship can be expressed as: Value of Money = 1 / Price Level, meaning as one increases, the other decreases proportionately.

 

• Statement iii, that it is 'indirectly related to the price level', correctly captures this inverse relationship, making it the only correct statement among the three.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This inverse relationship is a fundamental principle in monetary economics and underlies the Quantity Theory of Money.

 

• High inflation erodes the real value/purchasing power of money, which is why central banks like the RBI aim to control inflation to preserve the value of the currency.

 

NOTE

 

• None of the statements are correct (Option 1): Incorrect, since statement iii correctly describes the relationship.

 

• Only ii is correct (Option 2): Incorrect, as the value of money is indeed related (inversely) to the price level, not unrelated.

 

• Only i is correct (Option 4): Incorrect, since the relationship is inverse (indirect), not direct.

question: Mulayam Singh Yadav posthumously received the Padma Vibhushan in 2023. In which category did he receive the Padma Vibhushan award in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Public affairs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mulayam Singh Yadav, the former Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh and founder of the Samajwadi Party, was posthumously awarded the Padma Vibhushan in the 'Public Affairs' category in 2023. (मुलायम सिंह यादव — पद्म विभूषण, लोक कार्य श्रेणी)

 

• The Padma Vibhushan is India's second-highest civilian award, given for exceptional and distinguished service in any field, including public affairs.

 

• Mulayam Singh Yadav served as Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh three times and also served as the Union Defence Minister of India.

 

• He passed away in October 2022, and the award was announced as part of the Padma Awards 2023, declared on the eve of Republic Day.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards are announced annually and comprise three categories in decreasing order of importance: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.

 

• The Padma Awards are conferred by the President of India on the recommendation of the Padma Awards Committee, usually announced on Republic Day.

 

NOTE

 

• Literature and Education (Option 1): This is a separate category under Padma Awards, not the one for which Mulayam Singh Yadav was honoured.

 

• Art (Option 2): This category recognizes contributions to art forms, unrelated to Mulayam Singh Yadav's award.

 

• Trade and Industry (Option 4): This category is for contributions to trade/industry, not applicable to Mulayam Singh Yadav's honour.

question:
Which measure(s) is the Reserve Bank most likely to take to combat inflation in the economy?

A) Increase repo rate

B) Increase money supply

C) Decrease cash reserve ratio
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• To combat inflation, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) uses contractionary monetary policy, which involves reducing the money supply in the economy to curb excess demand. (मुद्रास्फीति नियंत्रण — रेपो दर में वृद्धि)

 

• Increasing the repo rate (Statement A) makes borrowing costlier for commercial banks, which in turn raises interest rates for consumers and businesses, thereby reducing borrowing, spending, and aggregate demand — helping control inflation.

 

• Increasing money supply (Statement B) would inject more liquidity into the economy, increasing demand and pushing prices further up — this is an inflationary, not anti-inflationary, measure.

 

• Decreasing the cash reserve ratio (Statement C) frees up more funds for banks to lend, increasing the money supply in the economy — again, an expansionary and inflationary measure, not a tool to combat inflation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• To fight inflation, RBI typically increases repo rate, increases CRR/SLR, and sells government securities (open market operations) — all measures that reduce money supply.

 

• Conversely, to fight deflation/recession, RBI decreases repo rate, decreases CRR, and buys securities to increase money supply.

 

NOTE

 

• Both B and C (Option 2): Incorrect, as both these measures increase money supply, which would worsen inflation rather than combat it.

 

• Only B (Option 3): Incorrect, as increasing money supply is inflationary, not anti-inflationary.

 

• Both A and C (Option 4): Incorrect, since though A helps combat inflation, C (decreasing CRR) works in the opposite direction.

question: Between who among the following did the Battle of Chandawar take place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaychand and Muhammad Ghori.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Chandawar (1194 CE) was fought between Jaichand (Jayachandra), the Gahadavala ruler of Kannauj, and Muhammad Ghori (Muhammad of Ghor) near the Yamuna river. (चंदावर का युद्ध — जयचंद और मुहम्मद गोरी)

 

• Muhammad Ghori defeated and killed Jaichand in this battle, which resulted in Ghori gaining control over key territories including Kannauj and Varanasi.

 

• This battle followed shortly after the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), in which Ghori had earlier defeated Prithviraj Chauhan III.

 

• The victory at Chandawar consolidated Turkish/Ghurid power in northern India and paved the way for the eventual establishment of the Delhi Sultanate under Qutb-ud-din Aibak.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Battle of Tarain (1191) was won by Prithviraj Chauhan against Muhammad Ghori.

 

• The Second Battle of Tarain (1192) was won by Muhammad Ghori against Prithviraj Chauhan, marking a turning point in Indian history.

 

NOTE

 

• Jaychand and Mahmood Gaznavi (Option 1): Mahmud of Ghazni's invasions of India occurred much earlier (11th century) and predate Jaichand's era; he was not involved in the Battle of Chandawar.

 

• Prithviraj III and Mahmood Gaznavi (Option 3): Prithviraj III's conflicts were with Muhammad Ghori (Battles of Tarain), not Mahmud of Ghazni.

 

• Prithviraj III and Muhammad Ghori (Option 4): This describes the Battles of Tarain (1191-1192), not the Battle of Chandawar, which was fought against Jaichand.

question: Which vitamin is synthesised in the presence of sunlight in our body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vitamin D.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vitamin D (also called the 'sunshine vitamin') is synthesised in the human skin when it is exposed to ultraviolet-B (UV-B) rays from sunlight, which convert a cholesterol derivative (7-dehydrocholesterol) into Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol). (विटामिन डी — सूर्य के प्रकाश से संश्लेषण)

 

• It is essential for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus in the body, playing a crucial role in maintaining healthy bones and teeth.

 

• Deficiency of Vitamin D causes Rickets in children (bone deformities) and Osteomalacia in adults (softening of bones).

 

• Unlike most vitamins that must be obtained entirely from diet, Vitamin D is unique because the body can synthesise it endogenously through sunlight exposure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin, along with Vitamins A, E, and K.

 

• Dietary sources of Vitamin D include fatty fish, egg yolks, and fortified foods, supplementing what is synthesised from sunlight.

 

NOTE

 

• Vitamin B (Option 1): This is a water-soluble vitamin complex (B1, B2, B6, B12, etc.) obtained from diet; it is not synthesised via sunlight.

 

• Vitamin C (Option 2): Ascorbic acid is a water-soluble vitamin obtained from citrus fruits and vegetables; deficiency causes scurvy, but it is not synthesised via sunlight.

 

• Vitamin A (Option 4): This fat-soluble vitamin is obtained from diet (e.g., carrots, liver); its deficiency causes night blindness, but it is not synthesised via sunlight.

question: Who among the following Indian grandmasters won India's first ever silver medal at FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Championship 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Koneru Humpy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Koneru Humpy, the Indian Grandmaster from Andhra Pradesh, won India's first ever silver medal at the FIDE World Blitz Chess Championship 2022, held in Almaty, Kazakhstan. (कोनेरू हम्पी — फिडे वर्ल्ड रैपिड एवं ब्लिट्ज चैम्पियनशिप 2022)

 

• This achievement made her the first Indian woman to win a medal at this prestigious blitz chess event, a landmark moment for Indian chess.

 

• Koneru Humpy is a multiple-time Women's World Rapid Chess Champion and one of India's most accomplished woman chess Grandmasters, having achieved the GM title at a very young age.

 

• She has consistently been ranked among the top women chess players in the world and has represented India in numerous Chess Olympiads.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Koneru Humpy later went on to win the FIDE Women's World Rapid Chess Championship title on multiple occasions (2019, and subsequently in later years).

 

• The FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Championship is organized annually by the International Chess Federation (FIDE).

 

NOTE

 

• Harika Dronavalli (Option 2): Another top Indian woman Grandmaster, but she did not win India's first silver at this event.

 

• Bhakti Kulkarni (Option 3): An Indian woman Grandmaster, but not the one associated with this particular silver medal achievement.

 

• Tania Sachdev (Option 4): An Indian Woman Grandmaster and chess commentator, but not the one who achieved this feat.

question: The stabilisation function of the government budget mainly includes _______.
option_2: intervention to expand or reduce the demand
option_4: distribution of income in society in a fair way
solution_text:
The correct answer is intervention to expand or reduce the demand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The stabilisation function of the government budget refers to the use of fiscal policy tools (taxation and government spending) to maintain economic stability by controlling fluctuations in aggregate demand. (स्थिरीकरण कार्य — मांग में वृद्धि/कमी)

 

• During a recession/deflation, the government intervenes to expand demand by increasing public expenditure or cutting taxes, thereby boosting economic activity and employment.

 

• During inflation/overheating, the government intervenes to reduce demand by decreasing expenditure or increasing taxes, thereby curbing excess spending and controlling price rise.

 

• This is one of the three key functions of a government budget, alongside the allocative function (efficient provision of public/private goods) and the distributive function (fair distribution of income and wealth).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The concept of the three functions of budget — allocation, distribution, and stabilisation — was propounded by economist Richard Musgrave.

 

• Fiscal policy tools used for stabilisation include changes in public expenditure, taxation, and public debt.

 

NOTE

 

• Allocation of resources (Option 1): This refers to the government's allocative function — ensuring efficient use of resources for producing public and private goods, not the stabilisation function.

 

• Production of public goods (Option 3): This falls under the allocative function of the budget, not the stabilisation function.

 

• Distribution of income in society in a fair way (Option 4): This describes the distributive function of the budget, aimed at reducing income inequality, not the stabilisation function.

question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the Deccan Plateau?
option_1: The Satpura Range is in the South of the Plateau.
option_2: The Eastern Ghats are in the East of the plateau.
option_3: The Western Ghats are in the West of the Plateau.
option_4: The Vindhya Range is in the North of the Plateau.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Satpura Range is in the South of the Plateau.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Deccan Plateau is a large triangular plateau in peninsular India, bounded by the Vindhya and Satpura Ranges to the north, the Western Ghats to the west, and the Eastern Ghats to the east. (दक्कन का पठार — सतपुड़ा उत्तर में)

 

• The Satpura Range actually lies to the north of the Deccan Plateau (not the south), running roughly parallel to the Narmada river and forming, along with the Vindhyas, the northern boundary of the plateau.

 

• This makes Statement 1 factually incorrect, since it wrongly places the Satpura Range to the south of the plateau instead of the north.

 

• Statements 2, 3, and 4 are all geographically accurate — the Eastern Ghats lie to the east, the Western Ghats lie to the west, and the Vindhya Range lies to the north of the Deccan Plateau.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Deccan Plateau is composed largely of basaltic lava (Deccan Traps), formed by volcanic eruptions around 66 million years ago.

 

• Major rivers flowing through the Deccan Plateau include the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri, all flowing eastward into the Bay of Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Eastern Ghats in the East (Option 2): This is a correct statement about the plateau's geography.

 

• Western Ghats in the West (Option 3): This is a correct statement about the plateau's geography.

 

• Vindhya Range in the North (Option 4): This is a correct statement, as the Vindhya Range forms part of the plateau's northern boundary.

question: In which dialdehyde are two formyl groups attached to adjacent carbon centres on a benzene ring and form fluorescent conjugation products with primary amines?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Phthalaldehyde.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Phthalaldehyde (o-phthalaldehyde, OPA) is an aromatic dialdehyde with two formyl (-CHO) groups attached to adjacent carbon atoms on a benzene ring. (फ्थैलेल्डिहाइड — बेंजीन वलय पर दो फॉर्मिल समूह)

 

• When OPA reacts with primary amines (in the presence of a thiol), it forms highly fluorescent isoindole derivatives, a reaction widely exploited in analytical chemistry for detecting and quantifying amino acids and amines.

 

• This fluorescence-based derivatization technique is commonly used in HPLC (High-Performance Liquid Chromatography) for amino acid analysis due to its high sensitivity.

 

• OPA is also used as a disinfectant and sterilant in medical settings because of its antimicrobial properties.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• OPA-based derivatization is a standard technique in proteomics and biochemistry laboratories for detecting trace amounts of primary amines.

 

• Aromatic dialdehydes like phthalaldehyde differ structurally from simple aliphatic aldehydes, as their reactivity is influenced by the aromatic ring.

 

NOTE

 

• Acetaldehyde (Option 2): This is a simple aliphatic monoaldehyde (CH3CHO) with only one formyl group; it is not a benzene ring-based dialdehyde.

 

• Valeraldehyde (Option 3): This is a simple aliphatic monoaldehyde (pentanal) with a single formyl group, unrelated to the described fluorescent reaction.

 

• Isobutyraldehyde (Option 4): This is a branched aliphatic monoaldehyde with a single formyl group, not an aromatic dialdehyde.

question: The folk dance of Chavittukali is associated with which of the following Indian states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chavittukali (also known as Chavittu Nadakam) is a traditional folk dance-drama form associated with the Christian community of Kerala. (चाविट्टुकली — केरल)

 

• The term 'Chavittu' means 'stamping of feet', reflecting the vigorous foot-stamping movements characteristic of this dance-drama form.

 

• It is performed by men and typically depicts stories from Christian mythology and European chivalric tales, such as the exploits of Charlemagne, blending local Kerala folk traditions with Western Christian themes.

 

• The art form is believed to have been developed in the 16th-17th centuries with the influence of Portuguese missionaries in Kerala.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important folk/performance art forms of Kerala include Theyyam, Mohiniyattam, Kathakali, and Koodiyattam.

 

• Koodiyattam is recognized by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.

 

NOTE

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 1): Notable folk dances of Andhra Pradesh include Kuchipudi and Kolattam, not Chavittukali.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 2): Notable folk dances of Uttar Pradesh include Raslila and Kathak, unrelated to Chavittukali.

 

• Gujarat (Option 4): Notable folk dances of Gujarat include Garba and Dandiya Raas, unrelated to Chavittukali.

question: The density of population of India as per the Census of 1951 is _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 117 per sq km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Census of India 1951, the population density of India was 117 persons per square kilometre. (जनसंख्या घनत्व 1951 — 117 प्रति वर्ग किमी)

 

• Population density refers to the number of persons living per unit of area (per sq km), and it has steadily increased over successive censuses due to population growth.

 

• The trend of increasing density is evident: 1951 (117), 1961 (142), 1971 (177), 1981 (216), 1991 (267), 2001 (325), and 2011 (382 per sq km).

 

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years, with 1951 being the first census conducted after India's independence in 1947.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per the 2011 Census, India's population density was 382 persons per sq km, with Bihar having the highest state-wise density.

 

• The Census of India is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

 

NOTE

 

• 324 per sq km (Option 2): This closely corresponds to the population density recorded in the 2001 Census (325 per sq km), not 1951.

 

• 103 per sq km (Option 3): This value does not correspond to any decadal census density figure for India.

 

• 382 per sq km (Option 4): This is the population density as per the 2011 Census, not the 1951 Census.

question: 'The Constitution of free India must be framed, without outside interference by a constituent assembly elected on the basis of adult franchise'. Who made this statement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru, on behalf of the Indian National Congress, declared that 'the Constitution of free India must be framed, without outside interference, by a Constituent Assembly elected on the basis of adult franchise'. (जवाहरलाल नेहरू — संविधान सभा की मांग)

 

• This declaration was made in the context of the Congress's demand for a Constituent Assembly to frame India's constitution, formally raised in the 1936 election manifesto/resolution of the Congress.

 

• While the idea of a Constituent Assembly was first put forward by M.N. Roy in 1934, it was Nehru who articulated this specific formal demand for a body elected on adult franchise, free from British interference.

 

• This demand was subsequently accepted in principle by the British government through the August Offer of 1940 and further discussions, eventually leading to the formation of the actual Constituent Assembly in 1946.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Constituent Assembly of India was finally constituted in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan, and it began its work on 9 December 1946.

 

• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the President of the Constituent Assembly.

 

NOTE

 

• MN Roy (Option 1): He is credited with first proposing the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934, but this specific formal statement is attributed to Nehru.

 

• Sardar Patel (Option 3): He played a crucial role in the Constituent Assembly and in the integration of princely states, but this statement is not attributed to him.

 

• Mahatma Gandhi (Option 4): While Gandhi supported the demand for self-governance, this particular formal declaration is attributed to Nehru, not Gandhi.

question: Which states are involved in the joint venture of Chambal Project?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chambal Valley Project is a joint venture between the states of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, developed on the Chambal River, a tributary of the Yamuna. (चंबल परियोजना — राजस्थान और मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• The project is a multipurpose river valley scheme comprising a series of dams, including the Gandhi Sagar Dam (Madhya Pradesh), Rana Pratap Sagar Dam, and Jawahar Sagar Dam (both in Rajasthan), aimed at irrigation, hydroelectric power generation, and flood control.

 

• The Chambal River originates near Mhow in the Malwa Plateau of Madhya Pradesh and flows through both Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan before joining the Yamuna in Uttar Pradesh.

 

• The project has significantly contributed to irrigation and power generation across both participating states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chambal River is also notable for the National Chambal Sanctuary, a protected habitat for the critically endangered gharial and Gangetic dolphins.

 

• The Chambal Valley Project's dams provide irrigation benefits and hydropower to both Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan and Haryana (Option 1): These states do not jointly operate the Chambal Project.

 

• Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh (Option 2): While the Chambal river eventually flows into UP, the joint venture project is between Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, not UP.

 

• Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): The Chambal Project's joint venture involves Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, not Uttar Pradesh.

question: Who among the following Indian Music composers won a Grammy award in the year 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ricky Kej.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ricky Kej, an Indian composer and environmentalist based in Bengaluru, won his third Grammy Award at the 65th Grammy Awards (2023) for Best Immersive Audio Album for the album 'Divine Tides', created with musician Stewart Copeland. (रिकी केज — तीसरा ग्रैमी पुरस्कार 2023)

 

• This win made Ricky Kej one of the very few Indian artists to have won multiple Grammy Awards, having previously won for 'Winds of Samsara' (2015) and for 'Divine Tides' itself in an earlier category (2022 announcement/2023 ceremony cycle).

 

• Ricky Kej is also known globally for his work in environmental advocacy and has been appointed as a UNCCD Land Ambassador.

 

• MM Keeravani, in contrast, won an Academy Award (Oscar), not a Grammy, in 2023 for the song 'Naatu Naatu' from the film RRR.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 65th Annual Grammy Awards ceremony was held in February 2023 in Los Angeles.

 

• India's other Grammy winners include Pandit Ravi Shankar, Zakir Hakeem (Ustad Zakir Hussain), and A.R. Rahman (for the Slumdog Millionaire soundtrack in 2009).

 

NOTE

 

• MM Keeravani (Option 1): He won the Academy Award (Oscar) for Best Original Song in 2023 for 'Naatu Naatu', not a Grammy.

 

• Aby Tom Cyriac (Option 3): He is an Indian recording engineer who has been associated with Grammy-nominated/winning projects in technical categories, but he is not the composer who won a Grammy in 2023 in this context.

 

• AR Rahman (Option 4): He won Grammy Awards in 2009 for the 'Slumdog Millionaire' soundtrack, not in 2023.

question:
Match the columns.

Name of Shifting Agriculture: i. Jhuming, ii. Dahiya, iii. Penda, iv. Kumari

Related State: a) Madhya Pradesh, b) Andhra Pradesh, c) North eastern region, d) Western Ghats
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-c, ii-a, iii-b, iv-d.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's shifting cultivation (slash-and-burn agriculture) is known by different local names in different regions. Jhuming is the term used in the North-eastern region (i-c). (झूमिंग — पूर्वोत्तर क्षेत्र)

 

• Dahiya (also known as Bewar) is the local name for shifting cultivation practiced in Madhya Pradesh (ii-a).

 

• Penda is the local name for shifting cultivation practiced in Andhra Pradesh (iii-b), also referred to as Podu in parts of the state.

 

• Kumari is the local name for shifting cultivation practiced in the Western Ghats region (iv-d), notably in Kerala.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other regional names for shifting cultivation in India include Podu (Odisha, Andhra Pradesh), Pama Dabi/Koman/Bringa (Andhra Pradesh), Kuruwa (Jharkhand), and Valre/Waltre (South-eastern Rajasthan).

 

• Shifting cultivation involves clearing a patch of forest land by cutting and burning vegetation, cultivating it for a few years, and then abandoning it to allow soil fertility to regenerate.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a): Incorrect, as it wrongly links Jhuming to the Western Ghats and Dahiya to the North-eastern region.

 

• Option 2 (i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d): Incorrect, as it wrongly links Jhuming to Madhya Pradesh and Dahiya to Andhra Pradesh.

 

• Option 3 (i-b, ii-c, iii-a, iv-d): Incorrect, as it wrongly links Jhuming to Andhra Pradesh and Dahiya to the North-eastern region.

question: Val Barker Cup in boxing is given to most outstanding boxer in the Olympics Games but it was NOT awarded in the Olympics Games _________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2020.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Val Barker Trophy is awarded to the most outstanding boxer, based on style, at each Olympic Games, and is considered one of the most prestigious individual awards in Olympic boxing. (वैल बार्कर ट्रॉफी — टोक्यो 2020 में नहीं दी गई)

 

• The trophy was NOT awarded at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics because the International Boxing Association (AIBA) had been suspended by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) ahead of the Games, and the IOC's own Boxing Task Force organized the boxing competition instead.

 

• Since the Val Barker Trophy is traditionally awarded by AIBA (now known as IBA), its suspension meant there was no recognized body to confer the award for the Tokyo 2020 Games.

 

• The trophy was reinstated for subsequent Olympics, being awarded again at the Paris 2024 Olympics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Val Barker Trophy is named after Val Barker, the first honorary secretary of the International Amateur Boxing Association (AIBA).

 

• Past winners of the Val Barker Trophy include boxing legends across various weight categories from different countries.

 

NOTE

 

• 2016 (Option 1): The Val Barker Trophy was awarded normally at the Rio 2016 Olympics.

 

• 2008 (Option 2): The trophy was awarded normally at the Beijing 2008 Olympics.

 

• 2012 (Option 3): The trophy was awarded normally at the London 2012 Olympics.
